claims.text: The target material is an FeNiCoCrAl high-entropy alloy in both a near-melting solid state and a fully molten state.
An additive cluster-expansion correction will be integrated into a standard EAM potential.
The many-body clusters used in the correction can be identified using elemental and binary-system data.
The proposed method is applicable from approximately 1300 to 1700 K.
The 1300–1700 K interval covers both the near-melting solid and fully liquid phases of the specified alloy.
Conventional EAM fails to capture relevant local configurational dependence in the alloy.
A cluster expansion can systematically represent the missing local configurational dependence.
Selected many-body cluster corrections will refine the EAM energy landscape to better reproduce the atomic configurations sampled by the ab initio liquid.
The refined energy landscape will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to standard TOR-TILD EAM references.
The cluster-corrected EAM will reduce the free-energy integration-path error by approximately 35–45% relative to standard TOR-TILD EAM references.
A residual free-energy error greater than 15 meV/atom relative to direct ab initio calculations will falsify the hypothesis.
The baseline consists of standard EAM potentials used in TOR-TILD without the proposed cluster-expansion correction.
Transferability to markedly different alloy compositions, bonding regimes, or temperature ranges has not been established.
The free-energy benchmark will compare cluster-corrected EAM thermodynamic-integration results directly with ab initio results between 1300 and 1700 K.
